# Theming

Every component paints from CSS custom properties. Nothing hard-codes a colour,
a radius or a duration, which is what makes a palette change one file rather than
a search across 39 components.

## The layers

**Primitives**, five seed colours and a warm neutral ramp generated by holding
cream's hue and decaying chroma toward the dark end, so a grey beside the brand
cream never reads cold. You almost never reference these directly.

**Semantic tokens**, the 36 names components actually consume: `--bg`, `--fg`,
`--panel`, `--border`, `--primary`, `--brand`, and so on. Each resolves per theme.

**Scales**, radii, durations, easings, z-index. Motion values are the ones most
often re-invented at a call site, which is why they are named rather than inlined.

All three are rendered live on [Colors](/docs/colors), read from the package at
build time rather than transcribed.

## Setting it up

One import, and one `@source` line:

```css
@import '@velobitsio/tokens/theme.css';
@source "../node_modules/@velobitsio/ui/dist";
```

The `@source` line is **not optional** on the npm path. Tailwind v4 does not scan
`node_modules`, so every utility used inside `@velobitsio/ui` goes ungenerated
and the components arrive completely unstyled, with no warning anywhere. `cva`
class strings survive into `dist` as string literals, which is what makes
scanning it work at all.

CLI consumers do not need it: the source is in your own tree, which Tailwind
already scans.

## Overriding a token

Redefine it after the import. Both themes, or the one you mean:

```css
@import '@velobitsio/tokens/theme.css';

:root {
  --primary: #0a6ebd;
}

.dark {
  --primary: #4aa3e0;
}
```

If you change a colour that appears in a contrast pair, **measure it**. The pairs
and their targets are listed on [Colors](/docs/colors), computed by the same
functions the CI gate uses.

## Three rules the palette encodes

**`--primary` is not a text colour.** `#007ACC` measures 3.86:1 on the paper page: fine as a fill behind white
text, and a WCAG failure as text. That is why there is
a separate `--primary-text` (spelled `text-link`), and why no `Button` variant
paints `--primary` as a foreground.

**Lime is asymmetric.** `bg-brand` with `text-on-brand` (charcoal) is 10.89:1 and
is the only sanctioned pairing. Lime _as text_ is 13.9:1 in dark and 1.13:1 in
light, so `--accent-text` is lime in dark and plum in light. They are not the
same token wearing two hats.

**Glass has two tiers.** Tier O (`.glass`) is for surfaces floating over
arbitrary content, dialogs, popovers, menus, toasts, sticky headers. Tier S
(`.glass-surface`) is for component surfaces whose backdrop is known to be the
page: `Card`, `Alert`, and the `Table`, `Accordion` and `EmptyState` shells.
Tier S carries **no `backdrop-filter`** by default, so a 20-card grid does not
mount 20 blur layers.

Forbidden on both: page backgrounds, and **nested glass**, two instances of one
tier composite about 2/255 apart and cancel each other out. Every surface-bearing
component takes a `surface` prop for exactly this reason; reach for it rather
than a `bg-*` utility, which wins the cascade and takes the material with it.

## Scrollbars

The import restyles **every native scrollbar** in your app, not just the ones
inside a `ScrollArea`: the document, an `overflow-y-auto` sidebar, a long line in
a `CodeBlock`. You get a 10px gutter, a transparent track, no arrow buttons, and
a pill thumb painted `--field-border` , the same bar `ScrollArea` draws, at the
same width, so a page that mixes the two shows one design and not two.

Six variables tune it, and because they inherit you can set them on any
scroller or on any ancestor of one:

```css
--scrollbar-size          /* gutter, default 10px          */
--scrollbar-inset         /* air each side, default 2px    */
--scrollbar-track         /* default transparent           */
--scrollbar-thumb         /* default var(--field-border)   */
--scrollbar-thumb-hover   /* default mixes toward --fg     */
--scrollbar-thumb-active  /* default mixes toward --fg     */
```

Two utilities:

**`scrollbar-none`** hides the bar. For a horizontally scrolled strip where the
affordance is content running off the edge. It does not remove the scroller, so
the region still needs `tabIndex={0}` to stay keyboard-operable.

**`scrollbar-on-dark`** for a surface that is dark in **both** themes , `bg-code`,
`bg-chrome`. The default hover and drag states mix toward `--fg`, which raises
contrast in light and in dark alike, but only on a surface that follows the
theme. On one that does not, the mix runs backwards and reaching for the thumb
makes it fade out (measured over `--code` in light: 4.58:1 at rest, 2.69:1 on
hover). `CodeBlock variant="terminal"` carries it already.

> **Do not set `scrollbar-width` or `scrollbar-color` yourself.** Setting either
> one on a scroller makes Chrome discard every `::-webkit-scrollbar` rule for it
> and hand back the platform bar, arrow buttons and all. Nothing warns. The token
> layer confines both properties to a Firefox-only `@supports` gate for this
> reason.

## Fonts

The token layer _names_ the typefaces and deliberately does not ship them:
`--font-sans` is `'Geist Variable', …` and the package stays dependency-free. Each
consumer installs the faces itself.

```css
@import '@fontsource-variable/geist';
@import '@fontsource-variable/jetbrains-mono';
```

Skipping this fails quietly: everything falls back to `system-ui`, the layout
barely shifts, and the only visible symptom is a glyph the fallback lacks
rendering as tofu. The `⌘` in `Kbd` is what gave it away here.

## Keycloak

The login theme takes tokens only, through
`@velobitsio/tokens/keycloakify.css`. It cannot consume `@velobitsio/ui`:
its component sources are git-ignored and re-vended by a
`keycloakify sync-extensions` postinstall hook, so an edit to an unclaimed file
is silently reverted on the next `npm install`.
